transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Session begins. Each player has Ysolde 3 FP, Aldous 3 FP, Morwen 3 FP, Mire 3 FP. Face-up: Endless Rain [H-01], Saint Orrin's Drowned Temple [L-02].

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: The rain has not stopped in eleven years and it does not stop now — it comes down in grey ropes, hammering the reeds flat and turning the ford's approach to black mud that sucks at every boot. Gullet Ford itself is a churn of brown water, faster and higher than any of you have seen it, with a single sagging guide-rope strung pole to pole as the only mark of where the crossing used to be safe. A hunched old ferryman crouches under a reed lean-to at the near bank, watching the four of you arrive from different directions along the same drowned road, sizing you up before he'll say whether he's still taking coin to guide anyone across tonight. Somewhere far off, past the tree-line, a bell that shouldn't still be ringing carries faintly on the wind from the direction of Saint Orrin's Drowned Temple.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: I know these waters, old man. The rope's holding, the ford's running high but not impossible. What's it going to take to get us across tonight?

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: (Ysolde approaches the lean-to with the easy stride of someone who's spent years on wet decks. Her eyes trace the guide-rope's tension first—reading the pull and strain the way the Stiltfolk taught her, before they cast her out—then she crouches to meet the ferryman's eye directly. There's no fear in her, only patient attention to the water's rage and the old man's silent reckoning.)

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: I know water, old man. Tell me what troubles you about this crossing, and I'll read the omens for both of us.

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: (Aldous approaches the lean-to, studying the water's movement and the guide-rope's tension, then the ferryman's expression. His fingers drift through the rain, reading its rhythm and weight.)

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: Can you take us across?

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: (Morwen steps under the ferryman's shelter from the rain and studies him directly, then glances briefly toward the distant sound of the bell tolling from Saint Orrin's before looking back.)

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: Old man, we're crossing tonight, whether the ford likes it or not. What's your price, and what do you need from us to make it safe?

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: (Mire steps forward through the downpour toward the ferryman's lean-to, moving with the confidence of someone trained in watch drills. She sizes up the ford and the old man, then addresses him directly and authoritatively—still speaking like she's badged, even though she's not anymore.)

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: "The water's afraid, old man, not angry. It rushes because it has nowhere else to go—but that means it knows where it's going. Look at how the rope holds despite the pull. Your ford is dangerous, but it's honest."

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Aldous refuses a compel.

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: The old ferryman just grunts at Aldous's talk of an "honest" ford, unconvinced by fine words when the rope groans against the current. Aldous holds his ground, refusing to let the man's doubt become his own doomsaying — he pays for that stubbornness out of his own pocket rather than let the water's fear become his. As he steps back to plant his feet more firmly, the bank does the arguing for the ferryman: eleven years of endless rain have turned the near approach to black soup, and the ground gives way under someone's boot. A pack skids toward the churn before hands close on the strap — nothing lost yet, but everyone's suddenly aware how little solid ground is left between them and the ford.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: There's a channel here, old man. I can read water the way my people taught me before they cast me out—let me show you where it runs safe.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: (Ysolde moves to the water's edge with confident steps, reaching down to steady whoever nearly went into the ford. As she pulls them up, her eyes never leave the water—she traces the guide-rope's tension, watches how the current breaks around the ford bottom, reads the pattern the way the Stiltfolk taught her before they cast her out. There's a safe channel here. She can feel it in the rope's angle, see it in how the water eddies and flows around the hidden shallows.)

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: "There. That's where the crossing holds strongest. The water's running true there—it tells you exactly where to place your feet."

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: (Aldous watches how the rain strikes the water, traces the current's pull on the rope and the ground beneath, and places his hand on the guide-rope itself to feel its stress. His fingers read the ford like text written in moving water. He turns and points to a line between the poles where the rope holds truest and the ground holds longest—where the flood has not yet eaten the bank away.)

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: Hold the rope and follow where I step. One at a time, no rushing.

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: (Mire strides forward into the black mud without hesitation, boots sinking as she tests the ground with deliberate, practiced care. She moves the way she was trained in watch drills—methodical and precise, feeling out solid ground beneath the rain-churned surface with each step. She plants her weight deliberately and turns back to the others, marking a path with her body.)

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Ysolde — create advantage with Notice: dice - - - 0, invoking Trained by a dead scholar [YS-02] → Average (+1) vs Fair (+2): SUCCESS MAJOR COST

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Aldous — create advantage with Notice: dice - - - + → Fair (+2) vs Fair (+2): TIE

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Mire — overcome with Physique: dice 0 - - + → Fair (+2) vs Fair (+2): TIE

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Ysolde reads the safe channel true — the party has their line across. But the shout and commotion of the near-fall carries across the water, and a Wardens toll-patrol working the ford's far bank comes splashing into view, torches guttering in the rain. Undermanned and frightened, they level spears and demand toll and papers before anyone sets foot on the crossing, F-03's clock ticking up as they plant themselves squarely in the party's path.

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: The water spoke plain, and I spoke plain with it — but I've named no more danger than what any soul needs to hear to cross safely. There's no priest here to pry anything loose from me.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Aldous refuses the compel on 'Truth Before the Dry Saint'.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: There. You see them? The reed-canoe—that's the way to read this ford. That's what I should have shown you all along.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Ysolde accepts the compel on 'Exiled from the Reed-Kin'.

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: The four of you make it across — but Gullet Ford takes its toll from each of you differently. As Ysolde points out the safe channel, one of the Wardens catches the old exile-brand on her wrist in his torchlight and barks an accusation of "swamp-witch business" to his fellows; she has to talk fast and loud to keep spears from turning her way, her Stiltfolk past dragged into the open right when she least wanted it. Aldous refuses to let the priestly compulsion loosen his tongue further, but his silence and old soldier's bearing only make the toll-patrol dig in — they levy a hard toll at the rope, coin and a share of the party's dry stores handed over before the Wardens grudgingly wave you through. Mire's careful path-finding gets everyone's boots on solid ground, but the driving rain has its own price: packs come across soaked through, salted meat and dry kindling ruined in the crossing. By the time the last of you stumbles onto the far bank, cold and lighter in the purse, the Wardens' sergeant has taken a long look at all your faces — and at Ysolde's most of all — before letting his patrol fall back into the reeds. Somewhere past the tree-line, the drowned bell of Saint Orrin's tolls on, indifferent to what the crossing cost.

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: Years ago, a hive-touched child was brought to his shrine for burning. I performed the old rites instead—the kind that calm without fire. He demanded I let the flames take her. I refused, and I got her to safety. He's sought me ever since.

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: I couldn't let him burn her. I still can't.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Morwen accepts the compel on 'The Exorcist of Hollowmoot'.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Beat: A Hollowmoot woman staggers up the bank ahead of you, soaked through and shaking, her eyes bright with a fever that isn't just from the rain — she's been drinking bad water for days and seeing things in it. She grabs at sleeves and coat-hems, babbling half in prayer and half in delirium, insisting she saw her boy walk into Saint Orrin's belltower with the swarm-song calling him, though the visions and the truth have started to blur together in her. begs the party to go to Not the temple itself first, she insists, dragging at Morwen's arm — the Drowned Priest holds a flooded shrine downriver from the belltower, and he's the one who calls the hive-touched home. She's heard the Priest's own people speak Morwen's name there before, like they were waiting for her, and she begs the party go there first if they want any answer at all about where the boy's been taken., because her son followed the swarm-song into the belltower.

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: The mother won't let go of Morwen's sleeve, dragging her off the causeway track and down a flooded footpath thick with reeds, insisting the belltower is a lie and the true answer lies with the Priest downriver. The rain slackens to a fine mist as the shrine comes into view: a half-drowned roof, candlelight bleeding gold through cracked shutters, and robed figures moving unhurried in the flood-shallows around it, as though they've been expecting company. One of them turns toward the party before a word is spoken — toward Morwen specifically — and murmurs something to the others that makes them go still. The mother's grip tightens, torn between hope and the fever-glassy terror in her own eyes, as she begs you all not to leave until someone tells her where her boy has gone.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: Ma'am, look at me—not at the water, not at them. The fever's making the truth run together with the fear. Your boy went into the belltower chasing the song. That part's real. Now tell me his name, tell me what he looks like, and tell me what you *actually* saw before the visions started.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: (Ysolde moves toward the fevered mother with the same steady grace she uses moving through a heaving night-barge—careful, grounded, attentive. She reaches out to gently steady the woman's shaking shoulders, meeting her fever-bright eyes directly. Her voice drops low, the way it does when a crew-mate is hurt or terrified: warm, unhurried, the voice of someone who has held secrets and heard confessions in the dark of midnight galleys. She's reading the mother the way she reads currents in dark water—finding the safe channel through panic and delirium.)

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: The rain stops, and they stand ready—waiting like men wait for a tide they know is coming. Tell me, mother: when your boy heard the swarm-song, was it in his head first, or did it come from the bell?

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: (Aldous steps closer to the fevered mother, one hand steady on her shoulder, reading the movement of the acolytes with the same intensity he'd use to read patterns in rainfall. His eyes sweep from the half-drowned shrine to the candlelight bleeding through cracked shutters, then back to the robed figures moving unhurried in the water—too unhurried, too patient. The sudden lull in the rain troubles him more than the downpour; he knows what silence like this can mean. He positions himself between the mother and the shrine, not threatening, but grounded and present.)

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: I'm not leaving her without an answer. If the Priest has something to say to me, he can say it now.

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: (Morwen steps closer to the fevered mother instead of back, one hand settling gently on her shoulder to anchor her. She doesn't look away from the robed figures who have turned to watch—doesn't hide, can't hide. She looks at the one who noticed her and keeps her voice level and quiet.)

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: Easy, mother. We're here now. But I need to know—are those the ones who took your boy, or are they something else?

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: (Mire positions herself between the fevered mother and the half-drowned shrine, settling into a protective stance with the weight-distribution and alertness of someone trained in watch drills. Her hand rests ready, and her eyes track the robed figures' movements—counting them, estimating distance, reading their stillness like she would any threat about to break. She's looking for weapons, for malice, for the tell-tale signs of danger that years of militia training burned into her bones.)

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: I know what I promised him, and it's been years. If he has something to say, I need to hear it — especially if it's about the boy.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Morwen accepts a compel.

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: The acolyte who marked Morwen steps from the shallows, robe dripping black, and inclines his head rather than drawing a blade. "The Exorcist," he says, tasting the name like a prayer. "We heard it from a pilgrim in Hollowmoot who wouldn't stop talking — Brother Fennic, wasn't it? Saved twice, he says, and grateful enough to shout your name to every soul who'd listen." Morwen's old debt has outrun her: Fennic's loose-tongued gratitude reached the Priest's people before she did, and now they know exactly who stands in their shallows and what she once refused the flames. The acolyte doesn't answer Ysolde's question about the boy — he only watches Morwen, waiting to see whether the woman who once denied his master a burning will beg, bargain, or turn away. Deeper in the shrine, something shifts against the candlelight, unhurried and patient, as if the Priest himself is finally rising to greet an old acquaintance.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: Your boy's name, ma'am. Say it clear—that one thing is real. Everything else, we sort after.

transcript.speaker: Ysolde
transcript.text: (Ysolde moves to the fevered mother with the careful grace of someone who's spent years on shifting decks, her hands settling gently on the woman's shoulders. She meets the fever-bright eyes directly, voice dropping to the low, warm tone she uses for crew in crisis in the dark of the hold—the voice that says: I have time, your fear won't shake me, tell me what's true. She positions herself to keep the mother's full attention fixed on her face, not on the shrine behind her, not on the robed figures waiting in the water. Just her. Just this moment. Just one clear name.)

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: The rain stops, and they stand ready—but your fever's running wild with more than just water sickness, mother. I need you to tell me what was real before the visions started clouding it.

transcript.speaker: Aldous
transcript.text: (Aldous keeps his hand steady on the fevered mother's shoulder, studying her with the same intensity he'd use to read patterns in rainfall. He traces the confusion in her eyes—fever-bright but grounded in real loss, real terror. His gaze sweeps from the shrine's waiting acolytes to the candlelight bleeding through cracked shutters, then back to her face. He's reading all of it at once: the fever, the fear, the truth beneath. Looking for the moment the visions started, where the real memory ends and the sickness takes over.)

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: Where is the boy? And tell the Priest my answer about the burning is still no.

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: (Morwen doesn't step back from the shrine or the acolytes. She keeps her hand steady on the fevered mother's shoulder, grounding her in something solid while the woman shakes with fever. She meets the acolyte's gaze directly, waiting—watching for the Priest.)

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: Morwen, we hold this line. Whatever debt you owe the Priest, we answer it standing—not on our knees. And the boy's mother doesn't walk out of here empty-handed.

transcript.speaker: Mire
transcript.text: (Mire pulls the fevered mother gently but firmly behind her, positioning herself fully between the shrine and the sick woman. Her hand settles ready on her weapon, and her eyes don't leave the acolyte or the darkness deeper in the shrine where something shifts against the candlelight. She's still holding the line, the way she was trained to do.)

transcript.speaker: Morwen
transcript.text: I'm not leaving. Not until he tells me where the boy is.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Morwen accepts a compel.

transcript.speaker: Table
transcript.text: Aldous — create advantage with Notice: dice 0 - + + → Superb (+5) vs Fair (+2): SUCCESS WITH STYLE

transcript.speaker: GM
transcript.text: Aldous doesn't let go of the mother's shoulder, and for one long breath he simply listens past the fever — past the visions of drowned saints and swarm-song choirs bleeding through her words — until the one true thread pulls clear: her boy didn't come this way at all. He went straight up the flooded causeway toward the belltower, chasing the sound, while she in her sickness followed a different voice down to the shrine. "The bell," she whispers, suddenly lucid, gripping Aldous's wrist like a drowning woman finding a rope. "It was always the bell." The acolyte watching Morwen goes very still at that — whatever answer he meant to trade for her old debt, the mother has just given it away for free, and there's nothing left to bargain with. He straightens, robe dripping, and delivers his verdict flat and final: "The Priest hears your answer, Exorcist. No is no. He remembers it." Then the robed figures withdraw into the shrine's black doorway without another word, candlelight guttering as if a door has shut somewhere deeper inside — no boy handed over, no blessing given, only the old debt marked paid in refusal and the party now plainly known enemies of the Drowned Priest's house. Morwen gets to keep her answer; the mother gets a true name for her grief and a direction to run in; and somewhere past the tree-line, the belltower's bell tolls on, closer now than it was an hour ago.

violations.issue: Aldous refused the compel offered on AL-04 (drawn for the tie at event 19). Per step 4, refusal means he pays 1 fate point AND 'the GM builds the cost from a face-up GM tag instead.' The FP payment was logged (event 24), but no subsequent event applies a cost built from a face-up GM tag (unlike event 23, which explicitly did this for the major-cost draw at event 16). The tie's mandatory 'success at a minor cost' complication was therefore never actually delivered.

violations.section: §6A (Draw triggers table, 'player accepts a compel that did not come from a deck draw')
violations.issue: The Story Pile draw for MO-05 (events 52-53) occurred only after the triggering compel (event 50) had already been fully narrated and accepted, so the rule's requirement that 'the complication must involve the drawn NPC or move the drawn thread' could not have been satisfied — the card wasn't drawn yet when the complication was fixed.

violations.section: §6A (Draw triggers table, 'player accepts a compel that did not come from a deck draw')
violations.issue: Same sequencing violation as event 53: the Story Pile draw for MO-06 (events 60-61) happened after the triggering compel (event 58) was already narrated and accepted, so the drawn card could not have shaped the complication as required.

ambiguities.issue: Arm A lists 'Attention', which the spec never defines.
ambiguities.detail: Arm definition lists Attention; not modelled.

ambiguities.interim_ruling: Fate Core: boxes 1 and 2; Physique/Will +1/+2 adds a 3 box, +3 or more adds 3 and 4.
ambiguities.detail: stress boxes built with Fate Core values

ambiguities.issue: Does a GLOBAL anchor give the GM a free invoke like a GM card?
ambiguities.interim_ruling: Yes, GLOBAL cards placed on the rail give the GM 1 free invoke that scene.

ambiguities.issue: Growth from 'roll fails after one of its tags was invoked' — invoked by whom?
Success with style on create advantage: the aspect's 2 free invokes AND the deck peek, or one of them?
ambiguities.interim_ruling: Both: the aspect keeps 2 free invokes and the player may also peek.

ambiguities.section: §4 (Resolving a drawn player card, step 4) / §3 outcomes table
ambiguities.issue: The spec doesn't say whether the deck draws for the major-cost roll (event 16) and the two tie rolls (events 19, 21) must be resolved in order before the next roll proceeds. Here all three draws (F-03, AL-04, YS-01) happened back-to-back before any of the three costs were resolved.
ambiguities.interim_ruling: Allowed deferred/batched resolution; each cost/compel event was matched to its triggering roll via the for_event/caused_by fields rather than resolution order, and no rule was read to forbid this.

ambiguities.issue: The rule says that when a drawn player card's compel is refused, 'the GM builds the cost from a face-up GM tag instead,' but the spec doesn't specify whether this must appear as its own logged event (as the major-cost path does at event 23) or can be folded into scene narration with no discrete mechanical trace.
ambiguities.interim_ruling: None was applied at the table for event 24; no discrete cost event was produced, which is logged below as a violation rather than resolved by a table ruling. Going forward the table should require a discrete Cost event mirroring event 23's precedent.

ambiguities.issue: Step 4 only specifies how ROOTS/REACH (player) cards should be interpreted when filling a blank (person/place or motive). It gives no guidance for a GM-owned card type (here HAZARD, H-05) filling a mismatched blank (WHO) after a type-mismatch redirect from step 3. The GM had to improvise personifying the hazard as 'a Hollowmoot woman' with no rule basis.
ambiguities.interim_ruling: GM was allowed to freely personify/narrate the GM card's tags to satisfy the mismatched blank, as long as one of its tags (here 'brings feverish visions') was used.

ambiguities.issue: MO-04 is a REACH card, which step 4 says 'becomes the motive,' but the type-mismatch resolution (step 3) forced it to fill the WHERE blank instead of WHY. The rules don't say how a REACH card's content should be reshaped when it lands on a non-WHY blank.
ambiguities.interim_ruling: GM blended the REACH tag into a location description (a shrine tied to the Priest who seeks Morwen) rather than a pure motive, treating the tag as flavoring the place.

ambiguities.issue: The written procedure has the card owner answer the GM's question (step 5) before the card's compel/surfacing (step 6). In the log, compel and surfacing for MO-04 (events 41-44) were resolved before the GM's frame question was even posed (event 45).
ambiguities.interim_ruling: Table treated the step order as non-binding; surfacing/compel happened first, GM's question followed once the card was live.

ambiguities.issue: The table's -1 row applies only when 'the party resolved a THREAT or filled a player's goal.' Event 62-64 applied -1 tension for successfully countering H-05, which is a HAZARD, not a THREAT/FACTION, and the scene notes don't identify a filled player goal.
ambiguities.interim_ruling: HAZARD cards were treated as equivalent to THREAT/FACTION for the -1 tension row.

cost_checks.note: draw_id field is blank in the cost list for this compel; no matching Draw event exists in the log for 'AL-01'. This is an ordinary hostile invoke/compel on an already-live binder tag, not a Session Deck draw, so the deck-draw tag constraint does not apply here and was correctly not treated as one.
Major cost (event 23) was built directly from F-03's own weakness tag 'Undermanned and Frightened,' satisfying §3's 'major cost must use its weakness tag' requirement.

The compel offer (event 24) correctly used AL-04's own weakness tag 'Priests pry loose any secret' per §4 step 2's default. friction.text: §4 step 4's fallback cost ('GM builds the cost from a face-up GM tag instead' when a player refuses the drawn-card compel) was not visibly executed for event 19/24 — the tie's guaranteed cost appears to have been quietly dropped after the FP payment, undermining the system's core promise that costs are never invented/omitted freely.

Three Session Deck draws (F-03, AL-04, YS-01) piled up from three separate rolls before any of their costs were resolved, making it harder to audit which cost belongs to which draw without relying on the for_event/caused_by metadata.

Heavily truncated notes text throughout the log makes it difficult to fully verify, from the fictional description alone, that each cost or compel text actually engaged with the drawn card's tag rather than generic scene flavor.

Story Pile draws triggered by 'accept a compel not from a deck draw' (events 50→52-53 and 58→60-61) are logged after the compel's complication is already written and accepted, making it structurally impossible for the drawn NPC/thread to inform the complication as §6A requires — this pattern happened twice in one scene.

The Beat Frame procedure's explicit step order (owner answers GM's question, §5 step 5, before the card surfaces and triggers its compel, §5 step 6) was inverted in play, and the spec provides no fallback for GM-owned card types (e.g., HAZARD) being forced into a WHO/WHERE blank it doesn't normally fill.
Tension was dropped for defeating a HAZARD card even though the §6 table's -1 row names only THREAT/FACTION resolution or filling a player's goal, leaving GM discretion undocumented as a rule.
